items.followUp: How many significant figures are there in 0.00450?

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of significant figures.
rubric.description: Defines significant figures as the certain digits plus the first uncertain (or doubtful) digit in a measured value.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the significant digits in 0.027.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct count.

modelAnswer: Significant figures are the certain digits and the first uncertain digit in a measured value.
In 0.027, the significant digits are 2 and 7; therefore, it has 2 significant figures.

items.followUp: What happens to the centripetal force if the speed of a body is tripled, while its mass and radius remain unchanged? Give a reason.

rubric.why: Checks the effect of doubling velocity on centripetal force.
rubric.description: States that the centripetal force becomes four times its original value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct change.

rubric.why: Checks the reason for the change in force.
rubric.description: Explains that centripetal force is proportional to the square of velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct reason.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is given by F = mv²/r.
If velocity becomes 2v, the new force is F′ = m(2v)²/r = 4mv²/r = 4F.
Therefore, the centripetal force becomes four times its original value because it is proportional to the square of velocity.

items.followUp: What is meant by gravitational potential energy?

rubric.why: Checks that elastic potential energy is identified as stored energy.
rubric.description: States that elastic potential energy is stored energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as stored energy.

rubric.why: Checks the cause of the stored energy.
rubric.description: States that the energy is stored when an elastic body is deformed, such as by stretching or compression.

modelAnswer: Elastic potential energy is the energy stored in an elastic body when it is deformed, such as when it is stretched or compressed.
